claims.source: U.S. Treasury sb0683: https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0683/, 2026-11-05.
claims.correction: Accurate for the collective concealment allegation. Treasury separately gives Greenmeadows-specific directorship and designation information.

claims.source: AGC updated Act 613, section 44 and separate targeted-sanctions provisions: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/3285881_BI/Act%20613%20%28Online%202026%29.pdf , as at 2026-03-01.

claims.claim: AMLA s.44(1): an enforcement agency 'may issue an order to freeze any property of any person' where 'an investigation with regard to an unlawful activity has commenced against that person' and it has reasonable grounds to suspect proceeds
claims.source: AGC updated Act 613, section 44(1): https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/3285881_BI/Act%20613%20%28Online%202026%29.pdf , as at 2026-03-01.
claims.correction: Once investigation commences, section 44(1)(b) alternatively permits suspicion of a specified offence or of proceeds/instrumentalities.
claims.stale_check: The complete test appears in the cited March 2026 text.

claims.claim: 'unlawful activity' includes a 'foreign serious offence' stated in a certificate issued by the foreign State.
claims.source: AGC updated Act 613, section 3 definitions: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/3285881_BI/Act%20613%20%28Online%202026%29.pdf , as at 2026-03-01.
claims.correction: The foreign-offence definition also requires conduct that would constitute a serious offence in Malaysia. The certificate condition alone is insufficient.

claims.claim: suspicious transaction reports and investigations are confidential under AMLA s.14A (prohibition against disclosure of reports) and s.35 (tipping-off).
claims.source: AGC updated Act 613, sections 14A, 35 and 79: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/3285881_BI/Act%20613%20%28Online%202026%29.pdf , as at 2026-03-01.
claims.correction: Section 14A protects reports with exceptions; section 35 concerns prejudicial disclosures. Section 79 supplies broader official secrecy, also with exceptions.

claims.claim: An investigation can stay confidential.
claims.source: AGC updated Act 613, sections 35 and 79: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/3285881_BI/Act%20613%20%28Online%202026%29.pdf , as at 2026-03-01.

source_assessment: Counting identifiable documents and articles rather than independent perspectives, the analysis cites 26 core items: 16 official/legal publications and 10 news articles. That convention includes seven claimed Malaysian coverage items, two ministerial reports and one trade-press article; it counts the two Singapore Customs pages separately. Ancillary notes additionally mention AFP's own copy, The Record, Kosmo, Apple and a 2022 ministerial report. The missing S/V source logs prevent a fully reproducible bibliography. Official material is concentrated in U.S., Malaysian and Singaporean executive, enforcement and regulatory institutions. Treasury, OFAC and the Federal Register often reproduce the same action; the Malaysian articles mostly reproduce AFP, so publisher count is not independent corroboration. The original confidence note says six Malaysian items were opened while other passages claim seven; this review reproduced six. Multiple languages and outlets are represented, but there is no substantive opposition, academic, NGO, community or affected-business perspective. Such voices are not substitutes for primary legal records, yet the missing company response, corporate registry extract, regulator interpretation and original ministerial statements limit the accountability narrative. The original also misses the Malagasy official custody announcement and later Singapore updates. The diversity score of 0.40 is a qualitative assessment, not a statistical measurement.
overall_assessment: As checked on 2026-11-18, the core U.S. designation facts, company identifiers, tranche counts and most historical chronology are well supported. The draft should not be published unchanged: its assertion that no source supports Chui's arrest is contradicted by an official Malagasy announcement; its Singapore comparison omits newer totals; and several Malaysian legal summaries need narrower, more complete wording. Public-search gaps cannot establish agency inaction, universal silence, bank relationships, STR filings or corporate ownership. The text generally preserves allegation-versus-proof distinctions and correctly separates Chui from the Prince Group tranche. Unverified findings indicate insufficient qualifying evidence, not presumed falsity; repeated factual propositions are consolidated, while rhetorical questions, analogies and self-ratings are not treated as independently testable facts. Belief masses follow the requested conservative calibration, treating republication of one institutional record as one evidential origin. The 78/100 score is a weighted editorial assessment of factual reliability, not an average of the belief masses. The material corrections rely on information available before the stated November 18 cutoff, so they are not hindsight criticisms.
